findings.title: U1 pin EN is floating / undriven
findings.failure_mode: A floating EN/CHIP_PU leaves the module in an indeterminate reset state — unreliable or no boot.
findings.citation: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 datasheet + hardware design guidelines: EN (CHIP_PU) must be pulled up (typ. 10k) with a delay cap; it must not float or the module may not boot reliably.

findings.title: U1 pin IO0 has no net for a required 100n
findings.failure_mode: A 1uF (instead of 100nF) cap on IO0 defeats the auto-download/reset sequence — can't flash without manual BOOT.
findings.citation: ESP32 auto-program circuit: IO0 uses a 100nF cap. A 1uF cap here (as on EN) is too large and breaks the auto-download timing.

findings.title: U1 pin EN has no net for a required 10k
findings.failure_mode: Missing EN pull-up => no defined power-on reset delay.
findings.citation: ESP32-S3 hardware design guidelines: EN uses a ~10k pull-up to 3V3 plus a 1uF delay cap (RC reset).

findings.title: U1 pin IO0 has no net for a required 10k
findings.failure_mode: Missing IO0 pull-up can leave the module entering download mode unexpectedly.
findings.citation: ESP32-S3 hardware design guidelines: IO0 (boot strap) needs a pull-up (typ. 10k) so the module boots to flash by default.

findings.title: U1 pin 3V3 is on 'Net-(R31-Pad1)', expected a net containing '3.3'
findings.failure_mode: Module supply off the 3.3V rail is out of spec.
findings.citation: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 datasheet, Pin definitions (3V3): module supply is 3.3V.

findings.title: DevKitC 3V3 output tied to external AP2112 3.3V rail via R31 (0Ω): two regulators in parallel
findings.detail: The DevKitC's 3V3 header pins (U1.1/U1.2) are the output of the board's own on-board 3.3V LDO, which runs from the 5V pin (U1.21 on +5V). Through R31 (0Ω) they connect directly to +3.3V, which U16 (AP2112K-3.3) also drives. So two LDO outputs are tied together with no isolation. The stored datasheet is a collection of Espressif board guides, and I could not find the DevKitC-1 power-supply section in it to quote.
findings.failure_mode: The two regulators will fight because their output setpoints differ slightly. The one set higher supplies all the current, and the other may be back-driven. This can make the current sharing and power-up order unpredictable, and back-feed one regulator when only part of the board is powered (for example, the DevKit powered over USB while the 5V input is off). If you meant the ESP32 to run from U16, remove R31 or leave it unpopulated and use the DevKit's own LDO, or feed only one supply path.

findings.title: U15 amplifier B (pins 5–7) not connected – unused channel left floating
findings.detail: Only channel A of U15 (OPA2810, dual) is used, as a unity-gain buffer driving CENTER_BIAS. Pins 5 (VIN2+), 6 (VIN2-) and 7 (VO2) do not appear in the netlist, so channel B's inputs are floating. This often happens when only symbol unit A is placed. TI's usual advice for an unused channel is to wire it as a buffer: VO2 tied to VIN2-, and VIN2+ tied to ground or mid-supply.
findings.failure_mode: The floating FET inputs of channel B can drift, so the output may rail or oscillate. This adds supply current and heat, and can couple noise into the CENTER_BIAS buffer and the ±12V rails.
findings.excerpt: VIN2+ 5 I Amplifier 2 noninverting input pin

findings.title: VREF/RFB driven by ±12 V op-amps right at the AD5452 ±12 V absolute maximum
findings.detail: VREF (pin 7) is driven by U4 OUT and RFB (pin 8) by U5A OUT. Both OPA2810s run from +12V/-12V and have rail-to-rail outputs. If either amplifier saturates (from a gain error, a fault, or startup), its output can swing to nearly ±12 V, which is the absolute maximum for VREF and RFB with no margin left. Confirm that the gained_func amplitude is limited well below ±10 V in every operating state, or add clamping.
findings.failure_mode: If an amplifier saturates or the ±12 V rails run slightly high, VREF/RFB can go past the ±12 V absolute maximum, which may damage the DAC.
findings.excerpt: VREF, RFB to GND −12 V to +12 V

findings.title: ILI9341 module datasheet unavailable; DS1 not checked against a datasheet
findings.detail: The tools could not find a datasheet for DS1, the ILI9341 14-pin SPI TFT/touch module. The pin connections could not be checked against a datasheet. Netlist observations for the engineer to confirm: VCC is on +3.3V. The LED backlight pin is driven directly by GPIO17, so confirm that the module has its own backlight transistor or resistor and check how much current the pin draws. SDO/MISO is not connected, so the display cannot be read back. The touch controller shares SCK/MOSI with the display and uses separate CS (GPIO18), DOUT (GPIO6) and IRQ (GPIO8) lines.
findings.failure_mode: Errors in the module's supply, backlight or interface would not be caught.

findings.title: TS5A23157 datasheet unavailable; SW3 not verified
findings.detail: No datasheet could be found for SW3 (TS5A23157), so I could not check its pinout, V+ rating, logic thresholds or decoupling requirements against the manufacturer's specifications. The footprint is a custom module (ohmen:TS5A23157_Module), so the pin mapping also needs a manual check.
findings.failure_mode: If the pin mapping or supply requirements differ from the datasheet, the DDS-to-function-generator signal routing could fail.

dropped.title: DevKit powered from both 5V and 3V3 pins; onboard LDO paralleled with AP2112 (U16)
dropped.detail:
U1 pin 21 (5V) is on +5V, so the DevKit's onboard 3.3 V LDO is running. U1 pins 1/2 (3V3) are tied through R31 (0 Ω) straight to +3.3V, which U16 (AP2112K-3.3) drives. That puts two regulator outputs in parallel. Espressif says the 5V pin, the 3V3 pin and USB are mutually exclusive power inputs. If USB is also plugged in, USB 5V back-feeds the board's +5V rail as well.

Second opinion (rejected): The netlist given does not show where R31 pin 2 connects, so the claimed tie to U16's +3.3V output is unverified; even if it is tied, both LDOs are fed from the same +5V rail, so neither can be reverse-biased while unpowered, and two 3.3 V LDOs in parallel normally just share or hand off load without damage, which makes this a guideline violation worth fixing but not a board-killing MUST-FIX.
dropped.failure_mode: The two LDOs fight each other: one back-drives the other, current sharing is uncontrolled, and the regulators can heat up or be stressed. If either regulator is unpowered, it gets reverse-biased.

dropped.title: U15 channel B (pins 5–7) not in the netlist, so the unused amplifier is left floating
dropped.detail: The netlist only has U15 pins 1–4 and 8 (channel A, wired as a buffer for CENTER_BIAS, plus the supplies). Pins 5 (IN+B), 6 (IN−B) and 7 (OUTB) have no connections. Either unit B of the symbol was never placed, or it was placed and left unconnected. An unused op-amp channel with floating inputs can oscillate or rail, which adds supply current and noise. Wire the spare channel as a buffer: OUTB to IN−B, and IN+B to GND (the midpoint of the ±12 V supply).
dropped.failure_mode: The floating channel B can oscillate or saturate. That adds supply current and heat, and couples noise into the CENTER_BIAS buffer in the same package.

dropped.title: U8 VREF driven by ±12V op-amp can reach the ±12V absolute max
dropped.detail: U8's VREF pin is driven straight from U4B's output (gained_func). U4 is an OPA2810 powered from +12V and -12V, and its output swings close to the rails. Gain is about 5 in U4A (1+2k/499) times about 4 in U4B (1+3k/1k), roughly 20x total. With that gain, a large input or a fault can push VREF to about ±12V, which is exactly the datasheet's absolute maximum and leaves no margin. There is no series resistor or clamp between U4 and VREF.
dropped.failure_mode: If the amplitude is set too high or U4 saturates, VREF could reach or exceed ±12V and damage the DAC. It would also clip the multiplied waveform.
dropped.excerpt: VREF, RFB to GND −12 V to +12 V

dropped.title: ILI9341 module datasheet unavailable; pin connections not verified
dropped.detail: No datasheet could be found for the DS1 ILI9341 14-pin SPI TFT module, so its connections could not be checked against the manufacturer's documentation. Two things should be checked by hand. First, the LED backlight pin (pin 8) is driven straight from GPIO17 with no transistor; check how much current the module's backlight draws. Second, SDO/MISO (pin 9) is left unconnected while T_DOUT is used for the touch controller, which means the display can only be written to and never read back.
dropped.failure_mode: If the backlight draws more current than the GPIO can supply, the GPIO could be overloaded or the backlight could be dim.

dropped.title: TS5A23157 datasheet unavailable; SW3 pinout not verified
dropped.detail: No datasheet could be found for SW3 (TS5A23157, footprint ohmen:TS5A23157_Module), so I could not check its pin mapping, supply range or analog signal range against the manufacturer's data. Here is what the netlist shows. V+ is on +3.3V and GND is on GND. IN1 and IN2 are driven by ESP32 GPIO21 and GPIO47. COM1 and COM2 come from the AD9833 outputs on U6 and U7. NC1 and NC2 go straight to func_in on each channel. NO1 and NO2 reach func_in through 39.2k resistors (R3 and R16), so each switch selects between direct and attenuated paths.
dropped.failure_mode: If the custom module footprint's pin numbering doesn't match the real device, the switch won't route the signal correctly.
